plan: Mechanism is equivalent to a second-price auction: highest sealed bid wins and pays the second-highest bid. With independent private values and risk neutrality, bidding one’s true value is a weakly dominant strategy. Overbidding risks negative profit by winning above value; underbidding risks losing profitable cases when the price would be below value. Therefore, I will set my exit price equal to my value ($30). If there’s a tie at 30, the winner is randomized; expected profit remains optimal.

In this two-stage format, your sealed bid sets your automatic exit point in an ascending clock, so the outcome is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction. With independent private values and risk neutrality, the weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value to avoid unnecessary losses from overbidding and missed profitable wins from underbidding. With value $7 and only one round (no learning), bid exactly 7. Ties are random, but bidding above 7 risks negative payoff; bidding below 7 risks losing profitable cases.

[ This is strategically equivalent to a second-price auction (winner pays the second-highest sealed bid). The weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value to maximize expected profit regardless of others’ behavior. Overbidding risks negative surplus if the second price exceeds my value; underbidding risks losing when winning would be profitable. No prior history to exploit this round. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value, $36. If there's a tie at 36, the winner is chosen randomly, which is acceptable given zero-profit at that price. ]
